about: The review app's model picker (server.py /api/models). The numbers come from MODEL_STATUS.md: the checks from "Every scenario kind: one model", the speeds from "Deployment". Keep the two in step.
speed: Per frame, one 1280 x 720 frame on the Ryzen 7 9800X3D and RTX 5070 Ti, measured per model size (small, full): GPU is PyTorch in batches of 16, CPU is ONNX Runtime fp32 on 4 threads, browser is onnxruntime-web on WASM.

checks.name: Tracking
checks.what: time on the bot minus the stats file's accuracy: mean, and mean size (nearer 0 is better)

checked_on: Recordings no model trained on, against their stats files (eval_moving.py).

full_v3.trained: Every scenario kind: static, dynamic, switching and tracking.
full_v3.best: The most accurate on moving runs: the most flicks measured on dynamic and switching runs, and tracking nearest the stats files.
full_v3.weak: 2.3 times small_v13's compute. On the Aim Lab upload it measures 8 fewer flicks than small_v11.

full_v6.trained: full_v3 fine-tuned on full_v5's checked crops and 309 robot crops checked by eye, one box per whole robot.
full_v6.best: Boxes a robot whole: Smoothbot Switch Robots matches 55 of 55 kills. Passes the acceptance gate against full_v3 (MODEL_STATUS.md).
full_v6.weak: Tracking a little farther from the stats files than full_v3 (mean gap size 0.141 against 0.117, within the gate's limit).

full_v8_s3.trained: full_v6 fine-tuned with the 2026-10-05 labels (crosshair, small targets, robots) and 354 health-bar crops checked by eye, with copies in other colors and without their text: a bar is never a target. Seed 3 of the recipe.
full_v8_s3.best: Tracking nearest the stats files of any model (mean gap size 0.099 against full_v6's 0.141), 4 more dynamic and switching flicks than full_v6, and no health bar taken for a target: Pasu Switch Wide 46 of 46 kills from the video alone (full_v7 35).
full_v8_s3.weak: Video alone a little below full_v6 (recall 0.9459 against 0.9463, precision 0.9608 against 0.9626). Targets as small as the crosshair: 1wall 2targets xsmall valorant 38 of 66 kills (full_v6 42).

large_v11.trained: The large model (1.8 times full_v8_s3's parameters) from scratch on every set, then fine-tuned with the Centering crops and the kills its first version got wrong against the stats files.
large_v11.best: Tracking nearest the stats files of any model (mean gap size 0.065 against full_v8_s3's 0.122, both with the hitbox test), boxes as wide as the targets, and 12 more dynamic kills found from the video alone.
large_v11.weak: Slower: 1.8 times full_v8_s3's parameters. 6 fewer dynamic and switching flicks measured, and the video alone a little below full_v8_s3 (recall 0.938 against 0.939, precision 0.968 against 0.970, both with the kill check).

large_v13e4.trained: large_v11 fine-tuned for 4 epochs with tiles labelled from the stats files' kills (no one drawing) and robot crops checked by Claude: the epoch-4 checkpoint of large_v13.
large_v13e4.best: Finds tiles large_v11 missed (Tile Frenzy 180 from the video alone: 195 of 212 kills against 152) and keeps robots whole; the video alone's recall 0.959 against 0.952, tracking's gap 0.062 against 0.065.
large_v13e4.weak: Switching runs: 3 flicks fewer than large_v11 (within the gate's limit), precision 0.915 against 0.919.

hand.label: Hand-written
hand.trained: No training: the rule-based finder in review.py. The first training labels came from it.
hand.best: Needs no model files and no GPU.
hand.weak: It assumes dark targets, so it fails on other colors and themes, and on a target under the crosshair (Pokeball scenarios).
